tagline: A mesa visible from US 191 gives Round Rock its name.
intro: US 191 runs north through the Navajo Nation, linking Many Farms, Round Rock and Rock Point before reaching US 160 near Mexican Water. Round Rock mesa is visible from the highway, rising 700 feet above the surrounding Chinle Valley terrain.

This northern highway was once SR 63. The stretch from Burnside to US 160 had been part of Bureau of Indian Affairs routes 8 and 17 before their transfer to Arizona in 1970 extended SR 63. In 1981, SR 63 became part of US 191’s extension south into Arizona.
Travel north from Many Farms to Round Rock, whose community takes its name from the nearby mesa. Continue through Rock Point toward the US 160 junction near Mexican Water.

moments.title: Many Farms
moments.text: Many Farms translates the Navajo place name Dáʼákʼeh Halání into English. The name describes the area’s farms, which became fully irrigated in 1937. US 191 meets BIA Route 59 here before continuing north toward Round Rock.

moments.title: Round Rock
moments.text: Round Rock’s namesake mesa stands 4.5 miles west of the community and is visible from Highway 191. The Navajo name Tsé Nikání means round flat-topped rock. Cliff-forming Wingate Sandstone rests above the slope-forming Chinle Formation, and the summit rises 700 feet above the surrounding valley terrain. Less than two miles north lies Little Round Rock, a butte.
moments.notice: Round Rock mesa is visible from Highway 191 west of the community.

moments.title: Rock Point
moments.text: Rock Point’s name describes the place where Chinle Creek enters high sandstone walls. US 191 meets BIA Route 35 here, then continues north to US 160 near Mexican Water.
